key_insight: Computational analysis identified three psoriatic arthritis synovial pathotypes: Dense Myeloid, Fibro-Stromal, and Angio-Lymphoid.
clinical_relevance: These tissue profiles may support future treatment stratification in psoriatic arthritis; this study concerns inflammatory arthritis, not cancer drug discovery.
method: Multi-modal staining of synovial biopsies from 61 patients, including 22 with psoriatic arthritis.
Digital whole-slide analysis and automated pixel classifiers quantified cellular and stromal features.
Unsupervised hierarchical clustering identified pathotypes and explored clinical and treatment-response associations.
evidence_signal: In the 22-patient psoriatic arthritis cohort, Fibro-Stromal tissue correlated with greater psoriasis severity; reported treatment-response rates were 44%, 50%, and 80% for Fibro-Stromal, Dense Myeloid, and Angio-Lymphoid, respectively, representing an exploratory trend.
watch_item: The small psoriatic arthritis cohort and exploratory response comparisons require independent validation before these pathotypes can guide treatment.
paper_title: Redefining Synovial Pathotypes in Psoriatic Arthritis through Multi-Modal Histology and Machine Learning (The PSYNOVIUM Study)
